ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At night the atmospheric heat-preservation effect is weak
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows the region from northern South America to near the west coast, marked with the 80° and 40° meridians and the 0° and 20° parallels; “Lima” is located near the Peruvian coast on the west coast of South America, and “Bing” is also in the Peruvian coastal area near Lima; “Yi” is located in the northern part of the continental interior, near the equator. Then reason: the area where Yi is located is relatively humid, with more water vapor and cloud amount in the air; Bing is located in the arid climate zone along the Peruvian coast, with dry air and little cloud amount. At night there is no solar radiation, and the ground mainly dissipates heat through longwave radiation. If there is little water vapor and cloud amount in the atmosphere, the atmosphere's ability to absorb the ground's longwave radiation and return heat to the ground is weaker, that is, atmospheric counter-radiation is weak. Therefore, at Bing the atmospheric heat-preservation effect at night is weaker, cooling is fast, and the day-night temperature difference is larger.
